title: fix(knowledge-turso): a build that continues after dropSource cannot bring the dropped source back
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cwPhGV4g9p1BGQaZbP

Fixes #37953

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：使用 Turso 知识库存储的部署里，删除一个知识源时如果别处还有一次对它的重建在跑，以前那次重建的下一页会把知识源悄悄"复活"；现在删掉的就没了，那次重建会被拒绝并停下。删除之后新开始的重建照常工作。
- 为什么做：这是 AI 知识库"索引分代与重建"专项的跟进，把 pgvector 存储上已经修好的同一个并发漏洞在 Turso 存储上补上，让两种存储行为一致。
- 出错会怎样：最坏的情况是一次正在进行的重建被拒绝，需要再重建一次；改动只在 Turso 存储里，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

`IKnowledgeAdapter.dropSource` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts`) removes "every generation, the one under construction included", and afterwards "a source registered again under the same key is built from nothing". On the turso store a build that was under way when its source was dropped broke that: its next page reached `writeTarget`, which found no generation and opened a new **active** one (the rule that a source holding nothing takes the first fingerprint it is handed), and the rest of the walk landed there. The contract sentence is right and is unchanged. The adapter is fixed, mirroring the pgvector fix that landed for the same defect class.

1. **A build carries the generation it began.** `beginBuild` now records, per source, the generation the build writes into: the one it opened, the one under construction it joined, or the active one it rebuilds inside. The record is the generation's number, the time its row was made (`created_at`, already a column of `knowledge_generation`, millisecond grain) and its fingerprint. The number alone is not enough on turso: the next generation is the source's highest plus one, so after a drop, or after one build replaces another, a new generation takes the same number again (pinned: a replacing build's generation is `2` again). Nothing new is stored; the table's shape is unchanged.
2. **A build's writes, listing and completion go only to that generation.** A call carrying `ctx.reason === 'reindex'` from a build this adapter began goes to its generation and to no other (`writeTarget`). When that generation is no longer active or under construction (the source was dropped in this process or another, or another build under another fingerprint replaced it), the build ends and the call is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` (409), the code and status pgvector answers. `completeBuild` makes the same check first. Before, a completion with no write since the drop threw a plain `Error` with no code.
3. **A page whose embedding was under way when the drop committed is written nowhere.** `writePassages` already re-reads the planned generation inside its write transaction; that check now also compares `created_at`, so a later generation under the same number is never taken for the planned one. The batch is planned again, and the build's retry is refused by (2).
4. A build that begins after the drop works as before: it builds the source from nothing.

turso has no builder lock and its drop is one SQLite-serialized transaction, so pgvector's first case (a drop missing a generation that a concurrent transaction opened) has no turso counterpart, as the card says.

**Serial with F6.** The approximate-index card (F6) edits the same file's search path and `completeBuild`'s start and has no PR yet. This PR stays out of the search code. A probe `git merge-tree` of this branch with that branch's head (`84f82932d4`) merges cleanly. Whichever lands second merges `main`.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in `src/__tests__/acceptance.test.ts` (the package's existing harness file), on `:memory:` and on a `file:` URL. Two adapters stand for two processes: each keeps its own builds, and on a file each has its own connection to the same database.

- A build beside the active generation, inside it, and of a source that held nothing, then a drop in the other process: the build's write, listing and completion (one cell each, 9 cells) are refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` 409; the store holds no generation row and no passage table for the source; `indexStatus` answers `{}`; a build that begins afterwards builds the source from nothing and is searched.
- A drop in the build's own process ends the build the same way.
- A page whose embedding was under way when the drop committed is written nowhere.
- A build another process replaced under another fingerprint is ended the same way, and the replacing build completes and is searched.
- A generation that takes a dropped build's number, under another fingerprint and under the same fingerprint made later, is never that build's.
- Through `KnowledgeService`: a walk whose source the other process drops after its first page stops (`ok: false`, `indexed: 100`, one page written), leaves nothing, and the next walk builds the source from nothing (`ok: true`, `indexed: 250`).

## Acceptance notes

- Boundary, not changed here: writes outside a build (`reason` other than `reindex`, event sync) are not fenced. One that arrives after a drop opens a fresh active generation, as for any source that holds nothing; the service stops sending them once the source is unregistered in that process. Same boundary as pgvector.
- Boundary, not changed here: the build's removals (`delete`, the walk's purge) are not fenced: they remove from every generation of the source, and after a drop there is none, so nothing comes back.
- Boundary: a build whose walk failed never calls `completeBuild`, and turso has no builder lock whose idle time would end it, so its record stays until the source's next `beginBuild` in that process replaces it. A capped walk (`limit`, no `beginBuild`) of that source in that process goes to the same generation it would have gone to anyway; after a drop it is refused once and the record is gone.
- Boundary: two generations of one source with the same number, the same fingerprint and a row made in the same millisecond cannot be told apart. That needs a drop and a new build of the source under the same fingerprint inside one millisecond of the first build's begin; such a build writes the same source under the same fingerprint.
- `buildEnded` text: one sentence, no SQL; operator text in `remedy`. No consumer parses it.

## Verification

Read first:
1. `turso-adapter.ts`, the `build` branch at the top of `writeTarget`: every call of a walk goes through it, and a wrong match would refuse a healthy build.
2. `completeBuild`: the check that comes first in its transaction.
3. `beginBuild`: which generation is recorded (the one under construction taken up first, then the active one, else the one opened).

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/knowledge-turso exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/__tests__/acceptance.test.ts -t "dropped while it runs"`. Expected: 30 passed (15 cells on each of the two store kinds).
